DUKE · NICHOLAS INSTITUTE · 2025
Rethinking Load Growth
Assessing the Potential for Integration of Large Flexible Loads in US Power Systems
Tyler H. Norris, Tim Profeta, Dalia Patino-Echeverri, and Adam Cowie-Haskell
Report NI R 25-01 · CC BY-NC 4.0
Read the report ↗
ABSTRACT (SUMMARY)
The study measures how much new, flexible load the existing US grid could absorb without building new capacity. It covers 22 of the largest balancing authorities, which serve 95% of US peak demand. Its key concept is “curtailment-enabled headroom”: new load that fits under planned peaks as long as it can be briefly scaled back during the tightest hours.
1.7–2.5 h
average length of a curtailment event
~90%
of curtailment hours still keep at least half of the new load running
PJM 18 GW
largest single region (at 0.5%), then MISO 15, ERCOT 10, SPP 10

India view
India is betting on sodium: no lithium imports needed
RELIANCE × FARADION
Jamnagar gigafactory
Bought UK sodium-ion pioneer Faradion and owns 100% since Oct 2024. Production planned from 2026: grid-scale BESS, commercial and telecom packs.
KPIT × TRENTAR
3 GWh cell line
KPIT's own Na-ion cells reach 100–170 Wh/kg. Technology transferred in Feb 2025, aimed first at electric two-wheelers.
WHY IT MATTERS
Sodium is abundant everywhere. That means cheaper storage without depending on lithium supply chains.
